tasks.title: Keep-warm worker and caller access the stop Bool without synchronization
tasks.discovered-by: independent review verified by main-agent full-file read
tasks.evidence-before: Ordinary Bool written by start/stop and read on a dispatch worker. Existing unchecked invariant claims stale reads are harmless, which does not make the Swift data race defined. keepwarm-tsan-red.log:153-235 records the actual race after an earlier invalid compilation attempt; only the running reproduction is RED evidence.
tasks.fix-summary: Both keep-warm types hold `running` as an `Atomic<Bool>` (Synchronization), stored with .releasing in start()/stop() and loaded with .acquiring by the worker loop. The stop/join semaphore still publishes `dispatches`; the cadence structure is unchanged and no timing claim is made.
tasks.evidence-after: AUDIT stage 2026-10-23: an independent reviewer read both types and found no remaining unsynchronized access. `startedAt` is written before the serial.async that is the worker's release edge and read only after the semaphore join, and `dispatches` is written only on `serial` and read only after `stop()` waits, so the semaphore -- not the atomic -- is what publishes it; .releasing/.acquiring is stronger than the kill flag needs. Latent, not live: `stop()` without `start()` or a second `stop()` would block on a drained semaphore, and a runner dropped without stop() is retained by its own `guard let self` loop; the only production call site stops exactly once. Fresh sanitizer evidence on the final tree: `swift test --sanitize=thread --no-parallel --filter GPUKeepWarmRunnerTests` exited 0 with 3 tests passed and 0 ThreadSanitizer warnings (AUDIT/aud2-020-tsan.log); the only later change to the file was a comment. The three lifecycle tests can fail on a missing join but cannot fail if the atomic store were dropped -- they pin the join, TSan pins the ordering. Commit 3842d8d (the TSan run compiled its parent).
tasks.disposition: Fixed on the branch at 3842d8d; not merged, released or verified on an independent host.

tasks.title: An occupied --port is reported only after the full model load
tasks.evidence-before: ServerArguments validates the port's range (1-65535, ServerArguments.swift:201) but nothing asks whether it is free. The server's only listener binds at HTTPServer.swift:125 from the call at main.swift:206, and that call comes after ModelRouter.preload() at main.swift:99 has loaded the initial install (36.9 GB for the default ornith15-8bit); with --lazy-load the load moves to the first request, so the refusal then lands in a request path instead. The L7 startup-configuration check the brief asks for existed for every option except this one.
tasks.fix-summary: Added ServerPortCheck.isAvailable(port:), a POSIX probe that sockets 127.0.0.1 with SO_REUSEADDR, binds, and treats only EADDRINUSE as unavailable. SO_REUSEADDR matches the listener, so a restart whose retired connections are in TIME_WAIT is not refused by the probe and accepted by the bind; every other probe error fails open, because the real bind stays the authority and a probe must not invent a refusal. main.swift calls it as the first act of the serving block, after argument parsing and the --catalog-only early exit, and exits 2 with the same 'error: ' shape the argument errors use. No load, preload or bind ordering changed.

tasks.title: Lazy disk indexing evicts a record loaded before the first index first, and latches done when the directory listing fails
tasks.discovered-by: independent checkpoint review of c5e2e93 (reviewer Q4), re-derived against the code by the main agent
tasks.evidence-before: Two manifestations, one cause. (a) load() inserts a record it finds on disk into state.disk and touchDisk appends it to an empty diskLRU before indexing has run; indexDiskIfNeeded then skips that key (`guard state.disk[key] == nil`) and appends the older records behind it, so the just-touched record sits at the LRU front and eviction removes it before records whose directories are older. (b) diskIndexed is set true before contentsOfDirectory is attempted, and its error is folded into an empty list, so one failed listing (root removed, EACCES, EIO) disables indexing for the lifetime of the store: removeAll then unlinks nothing and contains/metadata keep answering from direct lookup and an empty index. The turn store's loadEntries does not share either shape -- it is called at startup, resets the index, and retries on the next call.
tasks.fix-summary: indexDiskIfNeeded sets diskIndexed only after contentsOfDirectory succeeds, so a failed listing retries on the next call instead of latching; and it merges state.diskLRU with the indexed records by date -- the filesystem mtime for indexed records, the write/touch time for in-process ones -- instead of appending the listing behind a record loaded before the index. No format, budget or eviction-limit change.
tasks.evidence-after: RED on the pre-fix tree: AUDIT/aud2-046-red.log, 2 tests / 4 issues / exit 1 -- aRecordLoadedBeforeIndexingKeepsItsPlaceInTheLRU failed with the backdated record surviving and the newest evicted (three assertions), aFailedListingDoesNotLatchIndexingOff failed on the surviving directory after the root was replaced by a regular file for one call. GREEN after the fix: AUDIT/aud2-046-green.log, 30 checkpoint tests, exit 0. Full serial suite on the fix: 7 bundles, 1,995 tests, exit 0 (AUDIT/aud2-046-full.log); all 18 lint gates exit 0 (AUDIT/aud2-046-lint.log). The failed-listing fixture is deterministic (ENOTDIR), not permission-based, so it does not depend on the runner's Full Disk Access.
